UNITED STATES · 02:50 UTC

Trump confirms new limited U.S. attacks against an Iranian anti-aircraft system

Translated from Spanish · read the original →
The US and Israel opened strikes on Iran in late February 2026. The fight settled into weekly strike and counter-strike phases that narrowed to control of the Strait of Hormuz. A June memorandum lifted the dual blockades and opened a 60-day negotiating window. It collapsed on 8 July when Iran struck three commercial tankers and Trump declared the ceasefire over.
Trump confirmed new limited US attacks against an Iranian anti-aircraft system. They came inside the pattern of nightly operations that have targeted surveillance sites, military logistics infrastructure, underground weapons storage, maritime capabilities, an electricity plant and a desalination plant in Hormozgan province.
The conflict now turns on whether these targeted hits can degrade Iran's ability to close the strait without widening the exchanges back into the broader exchanges that ran from February through early July. Crossings remain at a three-week low and oil sits above 86 dollars a barrel. No pacification talks have restarted.
